# std/struct

> Struct declaration: struct Name ... end, one name: type field per line.

truck [std](../std.md) · [source](../../../registry/std/struct.pkg)

```
struct Point
  x: int
  y: int
end

struct Node
  value: int
  next: ptr Node
end
```

- Structs are top-level declarations and can be used before they are
  declared.
- A struct value lives on the heap: create one with `new Point`, which
  gives a `ptr Point` with every field zero (or `false`, or `null`).
- Variables, parameters, fields and slice elements hold pointers to
  structs (`ptr Point`), never struct values.
- Fields are laid out in order, each aligned to its size.

## Syntax

Kind: `struct`

```
struct {name: newtype} {fields: fields} end
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `name` |  | — |
| `fields` |  | — |
